title: Self-Hosted Image/Video Model — Cost Research Harness
purpose: Guided checklist to research the true cost of running our own open-weight image/video generation model on our cloud, so it can be compared against the hosted-API costs in 03-research-report.md.

research_summary.recommended_strategy: hybrid — hosted for production quality, self-host bulk/draft images on SERVERLESS only; do not self-host video for production
research_summary.critical_finding: Billing model decides the outcome. Pods/VMs bill wall-clock 24x7; serverless bills active seconds only. At 10k images/month a pod is 0.76% utilised (5.6 GPU-hours of work vs 730 hours billed).
research_summary.cheapest_image_path: RunPod Serverless L4 ~$0.00038/image (~₹0.036) at 2s/img — serverless, no idle cost
research_summary.pod_path_warning: RunPod L40S Secure pod = ₹68,656/mo fixed = ₹6.87/image at 10k volume, which is MORE than hosted Gemini batch at ₹6.37
research_summary.vs_hosted_image: Gemini 3 Pro Image 2K batch ₹6.37/image. Serverless self-host ~₹0.04–0.10/image; pods only beat hosted above ~8,600–10,800 images/month
research_summary.vs_hosted_video: Veo 3.1 Fast ₹71.25/clip vs Wan 2.2 serverless ₹14–28/clip, but 720p, no native audio, 5–9 min latency — not recommended
corrections_applied: First draft applied the serverless per-second formula to always-on Pods, understating pod cost by up to 92x
First draft applied a 70% utilisation divisor to Modal serverless, which has no idle tax
First draft treated AWS Capacity Blocks ($4.72/GPU-hr Mumbai) as pay-per-use; it is a prepaid reservation
First draft claimed breakeven ~0 for images; actual pod breakeven is ~8,600–10,800 images/month

conventions.currency: USD, with INR conversion at the rate captured on the research date
conventions.verification: Every price must come from an official provider pricing page; record the URL and the date checked
conventions.uncertainty: If a number cannot be verified, mark confidence 'low' and state the assumption instead of guessing
conventions.comparison_unit: Cost per generated image, and cost per generated 5-second video clip

sections.title: Which model to self-host
sections.goal: Shortlist open-weight image and video models that meet our quality bar and are legally deployable.
questions: Which open-weight image models are current as of the research date (FLUX.2 [dev]/[klein], Stable Diffusion / SD3.5, Qwen-Image, Z-Image, HiDream, others)?
Which open-weight video models are current (Wan 2.7, HunyuanVideo, LTX-Video, Mochi, CogVideoX, others)?
What is the exact model version and release date, and is it still maintained?
How does each compare in quality to our hosted baseline (Gemini 3 Pro Image, Veo 3.1)?
Does the model support the capabilities we need: reference images, image editing, image-to-video, character consistency?

sections.title: Is the model actually free to use
sections.goal: Confirm we can legally use the weights for commercial production output.
questions: What licence do the weights ship under (Apache 2.0, MIT, non-commercial, custom community licence)?
Is commercial use permitted without a paid agreement?
Is there a revenue or headcount threshold above which a commercial licence is required?
Are there restrictions on generated-output ownership, redistribution, or training derivatives?
Does the licence require attribution or output watermarking?
If a commercial licence is required, what does it cost and how is it billed?

sections.title: How big a machine the model needs
sections.goal: Determine the minimum and recommended GPU footprint per model.
questions: What is the VRAM requirement at full precision (fp16/bf16) and quantised (fp8, int8, int4)?
What quality loss comes with quantisation?
Does it fit on a single GPU, or does it need multi-GPU sharding?
What is the minimum viable GPU (L4, A10G, L40S, A100 40/80GB, H100, H200, B200)?
What is the recommended GPU for production latency?
How much system RAM, vCPU and disk are needed alongside the GPU?
How large are the weights on disk, and how long is cold-start model load time?

sections.title: How fast it generates — the number that converts hardware cost into unit cost
sections.goal: Measure or source generation time per output, since cost per image = GPU hourly rate ÷ images per hour.
questions: How many seconds per image at our target resolution, on each candidate GPU?
How many seconds to generate one 5-second video clip?
What batch size fits in VRAM, and what is the throughput gain from batching?
What is the effect of step count / scheduler choice on time and quality?
What speedups are available (torch.compile, TensorRT, xFormers, distilled/turbo variants) and what do they cost in quality?
What is the realistic GPU utilisation percentage in production, accounting for idle time between jobs?

sections.title: Where to deploy
sections.goal: Compare deployment models, not just providers — the serving pattern drives cost more than the vendor.
questions: Serverless GPU (per-second billing, scale-to-zero) vs always-on VM vs managed Kubernetes vs reserved/committed capacity — which fits our traffic shape?
What is our traffic shape: steady, bursty, or batch-scheduled overnight?
Does the DNA-generator pipeline allow queued/batch processing, which would let us run cheaper spot or scheduled capacity?
Does scale-to-zero cold start (model load time) break our latency budget?
Do we need multi-region, and does that multiply the idle-capacity cost?

sections.title: Which cloud and what it costs
sections.goal: Collect verified GPU hourly rates across candidate providers for the GPU classes identified in section 3.
providers_to_check: Google Cloud (A2/A3/G2, Vertex AI custom serving)
Specialist GPU clouds: RunPod, Lambda Labs, CoreWeave, Vast.ai, Together, Nebius, Crusoe
Serverless GPU platforms: Modal, Replicate deployments, Baseten, RunPod Serverless, fal.ai private endpoints
India-region options and their availability of the required GPU class
questions: What is the on-demand hourly rate for each required GPU class, per provider and per region?
What are the spot/preemptible rates and how reliable is availability?
What discount do 1-year and 3-year commitments give?
Is the required GPU class actually available in an India or nearby region?
What is billed on top of GPU time: storage, egress, load balancer, idle reservation, control plane?
What is the minimum billing increment (per-second, per-minute, per-hour)?

sections.title: Everything that is not GPU time
sections.goal: Capture the costs that make self-hosting look cheaper than it is.
questions: Object storage for generated assets and model weights — cost per GB per month
Egress/bandwidth cost for serving images and video out to users or CDN
CDN cost
Idle GPU cost: capacity paid for but not generating
Cold-start waste: GPU seconds spent loading weights
Failed/retried generations that still consume GPU time
Engineering time to build, deploy and maintain the serving stack — one-off and recurring
On-call, monitoring, logging and observability tooling
Autoscaling headroom kept warm for traffic spikes
Content-safety / NSFW filtering, which hosted APIs include for free
Model upgrade cost: re-benchmarking and redeploying when a new open-weight release lands

sections.title: Cost per image and per clip — the comparable number
sections.goal: Reduce everything above to the same unit used in 03-research-report.md.

sections.title: At what volume does self-hosting win
sections.goal: Answer the actual decision question rather than producing a raw cost number.
questions: At what monthly image volume does self-hosted total cost drop below Gemini 3 Pro Image batch (₹6.37/image)?
At what monthly clip volume does it drop below Veo 3.1 Fast 1080p (₹71.25/clip)?
How does the breakeven shift if we include engineering time?
How does it shift at 50% vs 90% GPU utilisation?
Is the quality gap large enough that a cheaper self-hosted image needs more retries, erasing the saving?
What is the hybrid option: self-host bulk generation, use hosted APIs for hero/final assets?

sections.title: Non-cost factors that can decide it anyway
sections.goal: Record the operational risks that a pure cost comparison hides.
questions: GPU capacity availability — can we actually get the GPUs when we scale?
Data residency and privacy: does self-hosting solve a compliance requirement that hosted APIs cannot?
Vendor lock-in and migration cost in both directions
Quality ceiling: open-weight models currently trail closed models on prompt adherence — quantify the gap
Fine-tuning upside: does a LoRA on our own DNA/brand data close that gap, and what does training cost?
Reliability and SLA: self-hosted has no vendor SLA; what uptime can we commit to?
Team capability: do we have the MLOps skill in-house today?

must_contain: Shortlist of self-hostable image and video models with licence status
Cloud GPU pricing table with official links and date checked
Cost per image and per 5s clip, in USD and INR, using the same 'per ₹100' / 'per ₹1,000' format as 03-research-report.md
Breakeven volume vs the hosted options
Clear recommendation: self-host, hosted, or hybrid, with the reason
rules: Follow 00-research-instructions.md: verify against official sources, state the verification date, exclude deprecated models, mark unverifiable data as uncertain
Every pricing row carries its official source link, as in 03-research-report.md
Focus on high-quality output tiers only; note excluded low tiers rather than listing them
